dct_description_sm: The legacy samples collected by DFO-FWI were analysed with the intention of determining what the MeHg speciation would be in different tissues and throughout the Arctic foodweb. Most monitoring data distinguish between different chemical and toxicological behaviors of inorganic Hg and MeHg, but none have addressed the fact that MeHg is not a single chemical species; instead, it includes CH3Hg+  complexes with various ligands that are known to possess markedly different mobility and biochemical reactivity. Once taken up through diet (e.g., zooplankton, fish), MeHg in marine mammals preferentially binds to sulfur-containing biomolecules. Exposed to marine animals, MeHg could be potentially neurologically available to the animal, as well as to northerners who consume beluga tissues as part of their traditional diet.
dct_subject_sm: Health sciences and contaminants -> Mercury speciation
dct_title_s: Chemical Speciation of Methylmercury (MeHg) in a foodweb of the Beaufort Sea Region
